{{Short description|Soviet and Moldovan mathematician}}

[[File:Vladimir Andrunakievich 2017 stamp of Moldova.jpg|thumb|upright=1.2|Andrunakievich on a 2017 stamp of Moldova]]
'''Vladimir Aleksandrovich Andrunakievich''' ([[Russian Language|Russian]]: Владимир Александрович Андрунакиевич; 3 April 1917 – 22 July 1997) was a Soviet and Moldovan [[mathematician]], known for his work in [[abstract algebra]]. He was a doctor of physical and mathematical sciences (1958), academician (1961) and vice-president (1964—1969, 1979—1990) of the Moldavian Soviet Academy of Sciences. Laureate of the [[State Prizes of the Soviet Republics|State Prize]] of the [[Moldavian Soviet Socialist Republic|Moldavian SSR]] (1972).<ref>[http://moldovanews.md/27062017/obshhestvo/154972.htm Математики отмечают столетие со дня рождения Владимира Андрунакиевича]. moldovanews.md (27 June 2017)</ref>

Andrunakievich was born in [[Saint_Petersburg|Petrograd]] and he graduated from the Faculty of Mathematics at the [[University of Iași]]. He received his Ph.D. from the [[Moscow State University]] in 1947 under the supervision of [[Aleksandr Gennadievich Kurosh]] and [[Otto Schmidt]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=106613}}</ref>

== Monographs ==
* Radicals of algebras and structure theory (with Iu. M. Ryabukhin). Moscow: Nauka, 1979.
* Numbers and ideals (with I. D. Chirtoaga). Kishinev: Lumina, 1980.
* Applied problems of solid mechanics. Kishinev: Ştiinţa, 1985.
* Modules, algebras and topologies. Kishinev: Ştiinţa, 1988.
* Constructions of topological rings and modules (with V. I. Arnautov). Kishinev: Ştiinţa, 1988.
